Probiotics and diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania: secondary analysis of a randomised clinical trial.

This secondary analysis of a randomized clinical trial in Tanzania examined whether Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation reduced diarrhoea morbidity in infants, and whether gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age predicted later diarrhoeal risk. The study links early-life microbiome profiles to enteric infection resilience, though the abstract does not report the direction or magnitude of the probiotic effect.

CAnDi: a global catalogue of anaerobic digestion microbiomes.

CAnDi is a new global database cataloguing the microbiomes involved in anaerobic digestion, the microbial process that converts organic matter into methane in bioreactors and natural environments. It compiles comprehensive taxonomic and functional information, including understudied components like bacteriophages and plasmids, to support research on these complex microbial communities.

Influence of Gliricidia sepium living support on rhizosphere bacterial recruitment and fruit metabolomics in black pepper (Piper nigrum).

This study used shotgun metagenomics and mass spectrometry to compare the rhizosphere microbiome and fruit metabolome of black pepper grown on living Gliricidia sepium support trees versus dead wooden supports. The living support system altered bacterial recruitment in the rhizosphere, with emphasis on Actinobacteria and antimicrobial resistance genes, and was associated with distinct metabolomic profiles in the fruit. The findings suggest that living support trees can shape beneficial microbial recruitment and crop chemistry in black pepper agroecosystems.

Assembly of minimally fragmented metagenomic pangenome graphs.

This preprint addresses the problem of pangenome variation graphs becoming highly fragmented when applied to metagenomic data, especially for hypervariable viral families. The authors propose an assembly approach that produces minimally fragmented graphs, allowing genomes embedded in different components to be compared more reliably. This improves the topological fidelity of graph-based comparative and evolutionary analyses in metagenomic settings.

Senimuribacter muris sp. nov., a butyrate-producing bacterium isolated from mouse feces, and reclassification of members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae.

The authors describe two new anaerobic, butyrate-producing bacterial strains isolated from the feces of laboratory mice, which they propose as a novel species, Senimuribacter muris sp. nov. Based on 16S rRNA gene and genomic comparisons, they also propose reclassifying members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae. This work expands the known diversity of gut-associated butyrate producers and revises the taxonomy of a bacterial family.

Taxonova: Deep learning enables fast and confidence-aware microbiome species-level amplicon classification.

Taxonova is a deep learning framework that classifies microbial amplicon sequences at the species level for both short- and long-read sequencing platforms. It addresses the limitations of similarity-based methods, which struggle with short amplicons and poorly represented taxa, by providing confidence-aware predictions across diverse amplicon lengths and variable regions.

Microbiome science needs AI competence, not just AI literacy.

The authors argue that microbiome researchers need deeper AI competence rather than just basic AI literacy, because common pitfalls like data leakage, incomplete metadata, ecological confounding, and unverified generative-AI outputs can produce convincing but biologically misleading conclusions. They propose a five-part AI-competence framework covering data and platform fluency, machine-learning competency, and related skills.

Microencapsulated immunoglobulin Y and lactic acid bacteria improve intestinal health in Yanbian Yellow calves.

The work supports microencapsulated IgY-LAB as a stable, effective strategy for reducing diarrhea-related morbidity and growth impairment in calves.
